summary: 1930 L-4 cab on Dollar Watch Mountain in the Pasayten, removed or destroyed in 1954; only remnants reported, reached by a 14-mile wilderness route.

facts.design: L-4 cab built in 1930 (FFLOS, firelookout.com); WillhiteWeb calls the 1930 building a cupola lookout house
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1954 (FFLOS says removed; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed). WillhiteWeb reports remnants but nothing large.

access.note: Wilderness route from Billy Goat Trailhead, 14 miles on foot. Sources describe the trail to the old lookout as likely unsigned.

visit.trail_note: Gravel road to Billy Goat Trailhead on Eightmile Creek Road, then about 14 miles on the trail through the Pasayten Wilderness.

events.note: A lookout's diary records a reported fire that was checked and found to be no fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com say an L-4 cab built in 1930. WillhiteWeb says a cupola lookout house was built in 1930. The Washington Lookouts page says an Aladdin lookout house. The story reports the differences and does not pick one.
FFLOS says removed. firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. The year agrees; only the word differs.
WillhiteWeb gives 8/6/1923. The Washington Lookouts page heads the same diary entry as December 1923, with the entry itself dated 8/6/23. The story says 1923.

sources.title: Dollar Watch Mountain Lookout - Pasayten Wilderness

notes_for_editor: Built year (1930) and removal year (1954) agree across FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb, but the building type differs by source. Firelookout.com lists personnel for 1929, a year before its own build date; left as stated. The only account of present remains is one photo caption on WillhiteWeb; the Washington Lookouts page quotes a second date, and the WTA trail page loaded without useful text. Brief coordinates (48.89553, -120.40725) match the FFLOS coordinates. Brief elevation 2340.6 m matches FFLOS 2,341 m. No new photos added (WillhiteWeb photo captions have no image URLs in the cache).
